title: Zscaler's AI Guard integration examples (zguard-ai-integrations): the catalog, the promised fail-closed posture against what each example does, and where each intercepts

prose.text: Zscaler publishes example integrations that call AI Guard's detection API from developer tools, gateways, agent frameworks, workflow tools and CI pipelines. This page lists them, sets the posture their documents promise against what each example's code does, and compares where each one intercepts. {{examples-not-product}}

checks.do: Read the specific example's handling of a missing key, a scan error and an unrecognised verdict before relying on it; the README's fail-closed table does not hold for every host.
Which events the chosen host can still act on after the fact (post-tool, Stop, afterAgentResponse): those paths see content the model or user may already have.
That AIGUARD_POLICY_ID is unset or a numeric ID the key can use; a malformed value is silently ignored and an unusable numeric one blocks everything.
That the installed zscaler-sdk-python is 1.9.44 or later.

das-pattern.statement: The root README's architecture section says AI Guard uses a DAS pattern in which each AI application integrates independently, with no proxy infrastructure required.

quotes: AI Guard uses a **DAS pattern** where each AI application integrates independently:
- ✅ No proxy infrastructure required
## Architecture: Detection as a Service (DAS)

client-kinds.statement: The Python examples call AI Guard through `zscaler-sdk-python`; the AWS components instead call the API with `urllib` and the standard library only, and the n8n node uses Node.js's native `https` module.

quotes: 1. Use `zscaler-sdk-python` **>= 1.9.44** when Python is available

**Exception: AWS.** Those components run inside Lambda and agent runtimes where adding a dependency is a deployment-package cost the user pays, so they call the API with `urllib` and stay stdlib-only.
The node makes direct HTTPS calls to the Zscaler AI Guard API using Node.js's native `https` module

sdk-floor.statement: Release 0.2.0 requires `zscaler-sdk-python>=1.9.44` for every Python integration, because earlier SDK releases never attached the Bearer token to AI Guard policy-detection calls and every scan failed with 401 Unauthorized.

quotes: **Breaking:** all Python integrations now require `zscaler-sdk-python>=1.9.44`. Earlier releases never attached the Bearer token to AI Guard policy-detection calls, so every scan failed with `401 Unauthorized`.

This switches the call to `execute_policy` against that exact id.

posture-table.statement: The root README says every integration fails closed: `ALLOW` is allowed, `DETECT` is allowed as monitor-only (reported and logged, not enforced), `BLOCK` is blocked, and a missing API key, an unreachable API, a timeout or network error, HTTP 401 or 403, an HTTP 200 carrying no `action`, and any unrecognised verdict are all blocked.

quotes: Every integration in this repository **fails closed**.
| `DETECT` | allowed — monitor-only: reported and logged, not enforced |
| No API key configured | blocked |
| API unreachable, timeout, or network error | blocked |
| HTTP 401/403 — bad or revoked key | blocked |
| **HTTP 200 carrying no `action`** | blocked |
| Any unrecognised verdict | blocked |
| `ALLOW` | allowed |
| `BLOCK` | blocked |

posture-exceptions.statement: The README names two exceptions: the Windsurf and Cline post-hooks and the Codex `Stop` hook are audit-only because those events cannot block, and unclassifiable gateway traffic is passed unscanned unless `failClosedOnUnknown` is set.

quotes: - **Windsurf and Cline post-hooks** and the **Codex `Stop` hook** are audit-only, because those events cannot block by design. They report and log.
- **Unclassifiable gateway traffic** — a request body no walker recognises — is passed unscanned unless `failClosedOnUnknown` is set.

soft-failure.statement: The example documents say a policy ID the key cannot use comes back as "Policy not found" inside an HTTP 200 with no `action` field, so reading a verdict-less 200 as permission silently disables scanning.

quotes: cannot use comes back as `"Policy not found"` **inside an HTTP 200**, with
no `action` field. Every integration here treats that as no verdict and
arrives as an HTTP **200** with no `action` field. Reading that as permission silently disables scanning while every integration still looks healthy.

transaction-id-uuid.statement: The example documents say the API answers HTTP 500 to a `transactionId` that is not a standard 36-character UUID; the 0.2.0 fix hashes such values with `uuid5` or omits them.

quotes: **The API requires `transactionId` to be a standard 36-character UUID** and returns
HTTP 500 for anything else
Fixed non-UUID `transactionId` values causing HTTP 500 — they are now hashed with `uuid5` or omitted

malformed-policy-id.statement: Across the Python examples a non-numeric `AIGUARD_POLICY_ID` is treated as unset and the call auto-resolves, so a malformed ID quietly applies the key's bound policy; only a numeric ID the key cannot use reaches the verdict-less 200 the README warns about. The Claude Code response hook is the exception and crashes instead.
malformed-policy-id.conditions: Chain over the hosts' parsing claims (each strips the value and returns None when int() fails). The legacy note called this inconsistent with the README's stale-ID warning; the code shows the two cases differ (malformed vs numeric-but-unusable), so it is not a contradiction.

direction-convention.statement: ARCHITECTURE.md defines direction `IN` as data coming into the system (user prompts, MCP tool parameters) and `OUT` as data going out (tool responses, URLs being fetched).

quotes: | `IN` | Data coming **into** your system | User prompts, MCP tool parameters |
| `OUT` | Data going **out** from your system | Tool responses, URLs being fetched |

agentic-guide.statement: The agentic AI guide labels an agent's prompt to its LLM direction `OUT` (to the external LLM), and its example agent scans that prompt with `OUT` and returns the generated reply without scanning it.

quotes: **Direction:** `OUT` (to external LLM)
if not self.aiguard.scan(llm_prompt, direction="OUT"): return {"error": "LLM prompt blocked"} return self.llm.generate(llm_prompt)

gateway-posture-exceptions.statement: The root README's statement that every integration fails closed does not hold across the gateway, cloud and framework examples at the pin: the Azure example policy sets FailOpen on the prompt leg, the Apigee inline proxy forwards JSON bodies without Gemini text unscanned, the SharedFlow passes unclassified traffic and harness-tagged requests unscanned, the Kong plugin returns unscannable responses unscanned, the Konnect callout passes when no callout response exists, TrueFoundry's error posture is set by the TrueFoundry guardrail mode, and the NeMo library flows would pass a verdict-less reply.
gateway-posture-exceptions.conditions: Each item is a code path in one example; the root README's own exceptions (Windsurf and Cline post-hooks, Codex Stop, failClosedOnUnknown) are separate. Not exercised against deployed gateways.

sdk-pins.statement: Of the SDK-based gateway examples, Portkey requires zscaler-sdk-python>=1.9.44 and TrueFoundry >=1.10.0 (for user forwarding), while the LiteLLM callback image and the NeMo install line leave the SDK unpinned; the AWS and Apigee examples do not use the SDK.
sdk-pins.conditions: A composition of the examples' requirement and install files at the pin; the changelog's >=1.9.44 statement (which says all requirements.txt files were pinned) is the parent's evidence for sdk-minimum.

fail-posture.title: What the host applications do when an example's hook crashes, times out or exits unexpectedly
fail-posture.detail: The examples' own handling is recorded per host (see the comparison table). Still open: what Claude Code, Cline, Windsurf and Codex do when a hook process crashes, times out or exits with an unexpected code (for example the Claude Code response hook's ValueError), and what the n8n node does with Continue On Fail off; only Cursor documents a switch (failClosed). No registered source states the hosts' behaviour.
fail-posture.blocks: whether a broken hook lets content through
